moves.reason: LL8's own resource pack, which upstream loads through paxi and this build loads from resourcepacks/ with everything else - one folder, one order, one list that locks them. The tree is upstream's and every release brings a new one, so it is moved rather than kept: keeping ours would leave upstream's copy beside it and the game would load the pack twice, and keeping nothing would put the layout back the way it was. Moved before the pins below, nine of which are files inside it.
moves.note: If a release ever ships it under resourcepacks/ itself, this becomes a no-op and says so; if it disappears from both paths the update stops rather than shipping a pack with the tree missing.

every resource pack of the build starts selected, in the build's order, and none is seeded as incompatible (the game deselects a pack it was told is incompatible and then finds compatible); the ghost JourneyMap/sophisticatedcore keys are gone; and there is no plate behind a name. EntityRenderer.renderNameTag takes the plate's alpha from Options.getBackgroundOpacity(0.25F), which returns the 0.25 fallback while backgroundForChatOnly is true and textBackgroundOpacity when it is false - so false plus 0.0 is the one setting that makes the quad fully transparent. It is the only pack-side lever that works on every shaderpack: Iris hands the plate to the entities_translucent program, and only three of the sixteen packs shipped here (Complementary Reimagined, Complementary Unbound, Lumina Lite) declare minecraft:name_tag and correct it themselves; on the other thirteen the plate comes out an opaque black rectangle over the name. The cost is that chat loses its dark backdrop, which is the same option. Refresh this copy when LL8 changes its defaults

this build's own datapack, seven files, and it exists because Jenny mod names biomes where it should name tags. Four of them replace the mod's own by the same paths and ask by tag instead - #c:is_overworld, #c:is_swamp, #c:is_floral, #c:is_nether - because this pack's overworld is largely Terralith's and the companions had almost nowhere to appear while their houses, placed by tag, were everywhere. A tag is only a valid biome list on its own: one inside a list is what the first version of this pack did, and the world would not open. The other three name the biomes the mod named itself, so nothing that used to spawn stops even where a tag turns out not to hold one

no waiting three seconds and standing still to use /home or /tpa. FTB Essentials counts a warmup down before it moves anybody and cancels it if they step off the spot, which is a rule for a public server and noise on a world four friends share. Every warmup in the file is 0, and 0 is not a short wait: WarmupCooldownTeleporter.teleport reads the number and, when it is zero, calls teleportNow instead of queueing a Warmup at all - so nothing is watching the player's position afterwards either. The cooldowns between uses are untouched. The whole file is pinned because it is upstream's and an update would put the threes back

the same datapack with one file mended. data_models/horse.json ships with a stray brace after its conditions block and the key "type" written twice in one object, so it is not json at all: Hostile Neural Networks logs it and carries on, and the model has quietly not existed. What the author meant is written the way every other mod in this pack writes it, a neoforge:not with the thing it negates under "value". It still does not load here, because it asks for naturalist to be absent and naturalist is installed - the twin file, horse_naturalist.json, is the one that loads. Mending it buys a clean log now and the right model if naturalist ever leaves; mending it by deleting the brace alone would have inverted the condition and loaded both

this build's own pack, five mobs whose model and texture came from different packs and did not agree. the marauder and the basher of Illager Invasion both bake the vanilla vindicator model layer, so EMF was giving them Gray's 128-UV vindicator.jem and Gray's compatibility pack was supplying 128px sheets to match - which worked, but what stood in the world was Gray's drawing of them rather than the mod's. vindicator is switched off in EMF now, so all three come back to the vanilla model, and the three 64px sheets they then need are here: the mod's own savager.png and basher.png, and Mojang's vindicator.png. the archivist and the necromancer are on the evoker layer and keep Gray's. and the older three:  skeleton.jem is Gray's skeleton - skull, jaw, ribcage and all - with the finger boxes from Skeletons Hands 67 remapped onto Gray's own 64x64 sheet, because that pack declared a 64x32 sheet and defined only the arms, so the vanilla skull and ribs came back and every arm UV read the wrong half. skeleton2.jem and skeleton.properties keep the joke: a skeleton named 67, six seven or sixseven still gets the second model and its wave, and it is now given sixseven.png by name, which the original never referenced. cow.properties pins the cow to the texture bound to it: Mugget's Standing Cow substitutes a 64x32 model and Gray's nineteen variants are painted for 128x128, so nineteen cows in twenty were scrambled. The two vex textures are The Backwoods classic's own 410x410 pair, put back above Gray's 64x64 pair, because the vex model in play is Backwoods' 410x410 one and Gray's ships no vex.jem to go with its art.

requested addition, kept through pack updates (Grays Mob Compatibility): 101 textures for 13 mods, redrawn from the vanilla layout onto the models Grays replaces. EMF gives a custom model to every entity drawn with the model it replaces, not to one entity type, so a mod's mob with its own 64x32 sheet was being stretched over geometry drawn by hand for a 128x128 one. Each face is taken out of the mod's texture and put into the rectangle Grays uses for the same box; the vanilla layouts came from executing the game's own mesh-building bytecode rather than reading it. Bees, spiders, illagers, ducks, wolves and the rest look like themselves again on Grays' bodies. The legs, antennae, stinger and wing dither were left unpainted in all 64 of them. Bees draw with an alpha cutout, so a uv rect with nothing in it renders as nothing, and every variant bee stood there with no back legs, stubs for antennae and half a wing. Measured against bee.jem - 150 uv rects, 1341 sampled texels - the redraw left 79 texels empty that Grays' own bee paints. Those 79 are copied across from it now, state for state, 5024 texels over the 64 files; the 23 empty in both are empty in the model too.

requested addition (gray's mob overhaul v13); last in the enabled list, so it sits above Cute Mob Models where both redraw a mob. The villagers are out of this copy: Grays redraws one whole - its own model, its own 128x128 skins, its own fourteen professions - and the model is not vanilla's at twice the size, every face carries a hand-placed UV and a sheep tail hangs off the body. A mod that adds a profession draws it the vanilla way on a 64x64 sheet, so Homesteads' five landed on whatever sat at those coordinates. The wolves are out for the same reason: EMF gives a custom model to every entity drawn with the model it replaces, not to one entity type, and Earth Mobs' skeleton wolf and wither skeleton wolf are drawn by the vanilla wolf renderer with their own 64x32 sheets, so they were stretched over geometry Grays drew by hand for a 128x128 one. Model, coats, collar, armour and the eye layer are out with it. The wolves are back: their redraw came out box for box, and the pack beside this one carries it. What is out for good is what no redraw survives - the slimes, whose second model reads the same file; the horse, a fifth of whose picture would be wings nobody drew; the blaze, eighty-five boxes where vanilla has thirteen sticks; the silverfish, with nowhere to put half the art; the vex, whose cloak loses its see-through; and the pig, which smears twelve to one. The sheep is the eighth, and it goes for the fleece rather than the body: a mod that colours a sheep does it with a layer baked from the vanilla wool model, and Grays draws that wool with 35 boxes where vanilla has 6. Earth Mobs' moss sheep redrawn onto it covers 36 per cent of the sheet - 77 of 210 faces with no art behind them - so the model goes back and every sheep-shaped mob is right again. The horse took four relatives with it and they were left behind the first time: a skeleton horse, a zombie horse, a donkey and a mule are the same body on the same sheet, and their models were still here after the pictures went. 117 files out for the villagers and 357 for those twelve, 1103 left, each byte for byte the author's

requested addition, kept through pack updates (ufo 2.1-fix7). Its own toml asks only for neoforge [21.1.216,) - this pack is on 21.1.248 - but the jar is built on Applied Energistics 2 far past what it declares: 118 classes reach into appeng and six mixins go straight into AE2 internals, CraftingCPUCluster and the CPU selection list among them. Both AE2 and Mekanism, which another 24 classes touch, are in the pack. CurseForge lists LDLib and Applied Mekanistics as required and neither is: Applied Mekanistics is referenced by nothing at all, and LDLib only by three classes under compat/jei, which is a JEI plugin and this pack ships EMI. The same gap means its recipes do not appear in EMI, because it has no EMI integration. The jar is the one CurseForge published, byte for byte. It registers quantum_pattern_hatch_menu twice - through AE2 build(id), which also queues the id, from inside a DeferredRegister that registers it as well - and that is what stopped the pack starting the day it arrived. Launcher release 336 rewrites the call to buildUnregistered as the class loads, so the jar stays as its author made it. The price is that this pack now needs that launcher to start at all: in any other one it dies on Adding duplicate key before the main menu.

the in-game disconnect timeout is five minutes, not one. A guest joining this world is frozen 16 to 56 seconds inside EMI reload while the host hands them the registry of 880 mods, and a keep-alive missed inside that window ends the session with a timeout - which is what it did to both guests on 25 August. requested fix, kept through pack updates (recipes lost to the rename): Minecraft 1.21 renamed data/<mod>/recipes to data/<mod>/recipe, and a mod that shipped for 1.21 without following ships recipes nothing reads - no error, no warning, an item that simply has no recipe and reads as uncraftable in EMI. Identity2 refuses a login whose UUID is an offline one and kicks a player whose auth challenge is late. Both are aimed at somebody else: the identities here are the launcher's, issued from a Steam account, and the lateness is EMI rebuilding its index for twenty seconds on the joining client - which is the moment the challenge arrives. A guest was thrown out of this world twice in one evening by it. The rest of the file is Identity2's own defaults. showDeathMorphRuleWarning is off with it, which is the other line that met every player at every login: To keep your morph after death, use /identity config set deathMorphRule none. It is advice about a setting this pack has already decided, printed to people who cannot change it.

Re:Animal replaces vanilla's pathfinding debug broadcast with a packet of its own, and that packet's writer indexes a path with no nodes: "Failed encoding custom payload the_black_blood:pathfinding_debug: Index -1 out of bounds for length 0". The encode fails, netty closes the channel, and the player is dropped to the title screen with Connection lost - the host of an empty world included, which is how it was found. This copy is the author's jar with one line gone from reanimal.mixins.json, the DebugPacketsMixin entry; every class, model and sound in it is untouched, and its other mixin still applies. When a release changes the jar the sha here stops the update, and the line is taken out again by hand.

requested fix, kept through pack updates (Server Side Horror 4.2): herobrine_starer_enable and starer_enable are off, and they are the only two settings in the mod that reach CommonClass.spawnFakePlayer - read out of ServerPlayerMixin.tick, where each is the gate immediately before the call (burn_down_house_enable is a third such gate, in stopSleepInBed, and was already false). That fake player is built without a network connection, so Connection.channel is null and anything that sends it a packet throws. On 2026-08-30 it cost two worlds in one evening: forty seconds of frozen server while CommonClass.getSkin waited on api.mojang.com from the tick, and then a NullPointerException through Artifacts and Accessories that Neruina caught on the player tick, kicking the host out of her own world and closing it for everyone. Everything else the mod does is untouched: the fake join and leave messages in chat, the dungeon arrival, the jumpscare, the signs, the lightning, the mining and footsteps, the traps, the heads and the sounds. random_fake_joiner_enable is off as well from 2026-09-01, and it is the same trap by another door: that one joins as a named player out of its own list and speaks a line from it some forty minutes later, and the server cannot encode what it says - no id for the minecraft:chat chat type in the registry that connection knows, because the holder the message carries came from somewhere else. Netty closes the channel it failed to write to, so every player is dropped at once: on the evening it was found, Projekt_M joined at 21:51, asked whether we wanted to be friends at 22:37, and both players lost the world in the same second. The plain fake_joiner, which only writes the join and leave lines and spawns nobody, is untouched.

requested fix, kept through pack updates (Yes Steve Model): DefaultModelId is empty, so nobody is given a model unless they pick one with F4. A player who has one is drawn by the mod rather than the game, and the mod draws only what the model has bones for - the built-in misc/2_steve and misc/1_alex have none for armour, and the only accessory the mod looks for is a Sophisticated Backpack, so full netherite showed as nothing at all. requested fix, kept through pack updates (pause menu): the build's own "Open to LAN" button is gone and the vanilla pause_share_to_lan_button is unhidden in its place - same anchor, same x, y, width and height, because the custom one had been put exactly over it. The custom button was a FancyMenu custom_button with an opengui action on ShareToLanScreen: it knows nothing about whether the world is open, so it never turns into the player-report button, and its own tooltip said as much - "Do NOT open to LAN again if you've already opened to LAN. Reason: The button won't be removed afterwards." The vanilla widget does the swap itself, which is what the launcher's one-press publish needs.

Yes Steve Model cancels RenderPlayerEvent.Pre and draws its own body, which costs the player every vanilla layer - armour, cape, Curios, Icarus - and, in a Jenny scene, leaves a second body standing in the middle of it, because the bus stops at whichever mod cancelled first and that is YSM. The server-side disable flag settles both: it is set while the chosen model is YSM's own Steve or Alex, which have no armour bones and are what a player picks when they want the ordinary body, and while the player is in a scene. YSM broadcasts the flag, so the armour is seen by everyone and not only by its owner

tomlEdits.reason: The switch that makes a Variant Bee wrong, held at off. The Bumblezone spawns sixteen pride-flag variants among ordinary bees, and its own text beside this key says to turn it on "if Variant Bee's model is messed up by another mod or resourcepack" - which is exactly what a player saw before Grays Mob Compatibility existed, because Grays Mob Overhaul ships assets/minecraft/optifine/cem/bee.jem and Entity Model Features hands that model to every renderer baking the vanilla bee layer, VariantBeeRenderer included. Turning it on moves the bee onto the_bumblezone:variant_bee#main, a layer no .jem here matches, so it keeps vanilla-layout geometry - and since the compatibility pack redraws all 64 variant textures onto Grays' layout instead, the fix from back then is now the thing that breaks it. Off is the only value that agrees with the packs this build locks on. The file is not pack-owned, so a player who already flipped it keeps their copy: this holds the shipped one, and only that.

requested change, kept through pack updates (C2ME): the client's render distance slider stops at the game's own 32 again. C2ME's client-uncapvd raises that cap to 97, which was worth having while the host's own distance was everybody's ceiling - a guest could at least draw further through Farsight's memory. Since launcher release 272 the shared world is served as far as the furthest player asks, capped at 32, so a slider that goes to 97 only offers a number the server will never send: it costs the guest's own frames and gives him nothing. The rest of C2ME is untouched, including the no-tick view distance that makes the served ring affordable.

Lootr's chests were invisible. The Backwoods classic pack, which this build locks on as the ground under everything, ships an OptiFine CEM model at assets/minecraft/optifine/cem/chest.jem, and Entity Model Features hands that model to every renderer that bakes the vanilla chest layer - Lootr's included, because LootrChestBlockRenderer extends the vanilla ChestRenderer and the Lootr block's own model has no elements at all, so the block-entity renderer draws the whole chest. The classic model is one box whose six faces all read from y=48..64 of the sheet, a band the classic pack fills in for the vanilla chest sprites and which is empty in every Lootr sprite - so the chest was drawn out of transparent pixels. With vanilla_textures on, LootrChestBlockRenderer.getMaterial returns Sheets.chooseMaterial straight away and the chests are drawn from the vanilla sprites the classic pack does fill in. What is lost is Lootr's own look for a chest somebody has already opened; the unopened particles stay, and they are the cue that matters.

count the hour of play, not the hour on the clock. Wall time keeps running while nobody is playing, so an evening away came back as time owed and the mod paid it the moment the world opened - a backup landing on top of world load, every session. This was tried once before and put back, because nothing was ever backed up: checkForTickCounterConfigUpdate converts the stored timestamp to ticks and then clamps it with Math.max(lastSaved, timerTicks), so with an hour's timer the first backup waits for the world's game time to pass two hours, and these worlds had minutes on them. The conversion only runs when the config and the world's saved data disagree, so the existing worlds were set to agree in advance with lastSaved already in ticks - nothing to convert, nothing to clamp. A world made from now on still meets the clamp once and gets its first backup at two hours

keep.reason: Resource packs this build added, which upstream has never had. A managed root is rebuilt from the staged release and whatever the release does not have is deleted, so every one of these went out with the next update. The other way to hold a file is a files entry above, which means committing it twice - once as the source, once as the target - for a pack nobody but us ships. Naming them here says the simpler true thing: ours, never upstream's, leave them where they are. Upstream's own ten are not listed: the release carries them, so the sync finds them and keeps them by itself.

Mods this build added by hand, which upstream's release does not carry. The sync would find them absent from it and delete them, and the overlay holds the other forty-two but not these ten. None replaces a file upstream ships, so keeping them cannot leave two jars of one mod behind - Biolith looks like the exception and is not, because upstream carries 3.0.10 nested inside Quark and this standalone 3.0.14 wins over a nested copy by version, which is why it is here at all. Create Aeronautics and Sable are one entry in two lines: the bundled Aeronautics jar carries aeronautics, offroad and simulated, every one of which requires sable [2.0.0,3.0.0), and it does not carry Sable itself - so losing either path takes the other down with it at load. They were out of the pack for exactly one build, to answer whether they were what stopped water being drawn. They were not.

jsonEdits.reason: requested change, kept through pack updates (Farsight): the render and simulation distance sliders stop at the game's own 32 again. Farsight replaces both OptionInstance ranges with (2, maxRenderDistance) in a HEAD injection on Options.load, which runs after C2ME's own cap-raise, so this number - not C2ME's 97 - is what a player's slider actually offers. Since launcher release 272 a shared world is served as far as the furthest player asks, capped at 32, so anything above that is a number the server will never send. It also took the SIMULATION slider to 64, and simulation is the distance that costs tick time - on a host that number becomes the world's. Farsight keeps doing everything else: the chunks a client has already received stay drawn when the server stops sending them.
